items.heading: Most People Think of "Joining
items.text: Most people think of "joining the Army" as one decision. It is actually several separate decisions bundled together: which service (Army, Navy, or Air Force), which entry route (NDA, CDS, TES, or Agnipath), and which commission type if you are entering as an officer (Short Service or Permanent).

items.heading: Before Comparing Entry Exams, Get
items.text: Before comparing entry exams, get this distinction clear, because it decides almost everything else - pay level, training length, command responsibility, and life path.

items.heading: Here Is What Each
items.text: Here is what each of the four main routes actually requires and how the process runs, side by side.

rows: Class 12 pass, unmarried, 16.5-19.5 years. Army wing accepts any stream; Navy and Air Force wings require Physics and Mathematics.

UPSC written exam (Maths + General Ability) twice a year, then SSB interview and medical. Selected candidates train 3 years at NDA Khadakwasla, then 1 year at the respective service academy before commissioning.
Bachelor's degree in any discipline. Age band differs by academy: roughly 19-24 for IMA, 19-22 for INA, 19-23 for AFA, and 19-25 for OTA (non-technical, no pension track).
UPSC written exam twice a year, then SSB and medical. Training runs 1-1.5 years depending on the academy before commissioning as an officer.
Class 12 pass with Physics, Chemistry, Maths (60%+), unmarried, 16.5-19.5 years. Selection uses your JEE Main score directly.

No separate written exam from the Army. Shortlisting on JEE Main score, then SSB and medical. Selected candidates get a fully funded 4-year B.Tech at an Army engineering college, commissioned as Lieutenant on completion.
10th or 12th pass depending on trade, 17.5-21 years for Navy and 17.5-23 years for Army and Air Force. Open to men and women depending on service and trade.
Written/online test, physical fitness test, medical, and merit list. Selected candidates serve a fixed 4-year tenure; up to 25% are retained for full regular service afterward.
